edges.why: A Rubin GPU package must join its compute dies and HBM4 memory; the exact Rubin package flow is not fully disclosed here.
Package assembly follows fabrication of the GPU logic dies.
The packaged compute and memory dies form the Rubin GPU component.
NVIDIA describes Rubin systems and racks as liquid-cooled.
AI factory deployment requires electrical service and distribution; Rubin-specific power capacity is not quantified here.
NVIDIA describes global supply-chain leaders and more than 80 MGX ecosystem partners around Vera Rubin.
NVIDIA identifies HBM3E as a Blackwell memory capability.
NVIDIA describes fifth-generation NVLink and switch technology for Blackwell.
BlueField-4 is part of Rubin’s AI-native storage and infrastructure path.
ConnectX-9 is part of the scale-out networking layer in the Rubin platform.
Micron and SK hynix publicly connect their advanced memory work to Vera Rubin; this does not establish exclusivity.
NVIDIA describes NVL72 as a liquid-cooled rack-scale system.
Rubin GPU logic must be fabricated before package assembly; the manufacturing supplier is not named here.
NVIDIA specifies HBM4 12-Hi stacks while supplier sources establish HBM4 production and development paths.
The 12-Hi stack is the specified Rubin HBM4 configuration described by NVIDIA.
Each NVL72 integrates 72 Rubin GPUs according to NVIDIA’s platform description.
Each NVL72 integrates 36 Vera CPUs according to NVIDIA’s platform description.
NVLink 6 connects the GPUs in the Rubin rack-scale domain.
ConnectX-9 SuperNICs are listed as part of NVL72.
BlueField-4 DPUs are listed as part of the Rubin rack platform.
The Rubin rack is described as liquid-cooled; the facility-side implementation remains deployment-specific.
NVL72 is a rack-scale building block for NVIDIA AI factories.
NVIDIA describes Rubin with HBM4 memory, up to 288 GB and 22 TB/s per GPU.
Rubin uses NVLink 6 for GPU-to-GPU scale-up communication.
NVIDIA positions Rubin as the next platform generation after Blackwell; exact supply-chain changes must be read from the documented components.
NVIDIA documents HBM4 for Rubin and HBM3E for Blackwell; that establishes an architecture comparison, not a supplier-level replacement path.
NVIDIA describes Rubin with sixth-generation NVLink and Blackwell with fifth-generation NVLink.
NVIDIA says Taiwan server makers and global supply-chain leaders are manufacturing and shipping Rubin-based systems, but does not establish which partner makes or ships NVL72 specifically.
Spectrum-6 is the Rubin scale-out Ethernet layer for rack-to-rack connectivity.
NVIDIA describes Spectrum-X Ethernet Photonics as a co-packaged optical path within the Rubin networking platform.
A photonic scale-out network requires optical components, packaging and facility fiber; the exact Rubin supplier chain is not established here.
The Rubin GPU is one of the named chips in the Vera Rubin platform.
The Vera CPU is one of the named chips in the Vera Rubin platform.
Vera Rubin is documented as a rack-scale platform with NVL72 systems.
